changes: No substantive changes. I expanded the notes on the author's surname and epithet, on the absence of copy data, and on 'likhidisva'.

notes: The only person named is the author. The colophon calls him Kāśīnātha 'bhaṭṭopanāmaka', meaning his surname (upanāma) is Bhaṭṭa, and gives him the epithet 'dakṣiṇāmūrti-śivārādhaka' (worshipper of Śiva as Dakṣiṇāmūrti; 'śīva' is a slip for 'śiva'). He is probably Kāśīnātha Bhaṭṭa (Śivānandanātha), the late Tantric compiler, but the colophon does not say so. Bhaṭṭa is recorded as a surname-title. The colophon closes the uttarārdha with the stock 'ādarśadoṣā...' and '...kṣamasva' formulas but names no scribe, patron, date or place. 'likhidisva' is corrupt, probably for likhitvā or likhitam.
